findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The audit-log endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime" where the key is a datetime object, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via strftime/timestamp. Any request to OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint with optimized_pagination=true will crash instead of paginating.

findings.title: Client-controlled negative offset passed to queryset slicing
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 it sets start_offset = cursor.offset and does queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string and Django QuerySet explicitly forbids negative indexing and raises AssertionError, so a crafted cursor causes an unhandled 500. The comment claiming Django properly handles negative slicing automatically and that it is safe because permissions are checked at queryset level is false; it enables denial of service and establishes an unsafe pagination primitive.

findings.title: BasePaginator now allows negative slice on prev path
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result was changed to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. Offset is attacker-controlled via Cursor.from_string. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is now passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django rejects with AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported, turning a bad cursor into a 500. For forward cursors the same bad input is silently clamped to 0 and returns the first page, so behavior is inconsistent and boundary validation is lost.

findings.title: Unknown paginate kwarg breaks optimized path
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the optimized branch calls self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, ..., enable_advanced_features=True). Base endpoint paginate does not define an enable_advanced_features parameter; it constructs the paginator itself. Passing a paginator-specific constructor argument through paginate will raise TypeError for unexpected keyword argument, so every request with optimized_pagination=true fails with 500 instead of returning audit logs.
